results.title: When we first started building Dodo Payments and piecing out what we wanted from the product, I told Ayush that we should have an absolutely seamless experience for the end user. Our focus has… | Rishabh Goel
results.content: #The Broken Button That Wasn’t Broken A few years ago, I joined a team working on a mobile app for booking cabs. One day, customer complaints started pouring in — “The Confirm Ride button doesn’t work!” The team panicked. Designers checked the layout, developers reviewed the code, testers ran multiple builds — everything looked fine.Still, users kept complaining. So, instead of staring at dashboards, I called a few users. One of them said, “I keep tapping Confirm, but it doesn’t do anything.” I asked her to walk me through it — and that’s when I noticed something subtle: the app took 8 seconds to load fare details before activating the button. The button wasn’t broken — it was just slow. Our fix wasn’t new code; it was adding a simple loading message: “Fetching fare details…” Complaints [...] simple loading message: “Fetching fare details…” Complaints dropped by 90% the next day. That experience taught me something I’ll never forget: "Users don’t always describe the problem correctly — it’s our job to listen between the lines." Product Management isn’t just about building features or fixing bugs; it’s about discovering the truth behind the feedback. Sometimes, solving the problem means understanding the emotion, not just the error. #productmanagement #learnings

## Grace Periods and Payment Update Flows

A grace period is a window of time where a customer maintains access to your product even though their payment has failed. This is crucial for maintaining a good billing UX.

If a developer’s API key stops working the second a payment fails, you’ve just broken their application. They’ll be frustrated and might look for an alternative. If you give them a 7-day grace period, you give them time to fix the issue without service interruption.

### The Recovery Funnel
